summary: One strong mechanical policy (human approval before git push), several 'run the generator after changing X' rules that are checkable but point the opposite way from require-before, and a large body of command reference and directory tables that describe the repository rather than constrain the agent.

policies.quote: Before running `git push`, stop and get explicit human approval.
policies.note: The clearest rule in the document, and the one a live trial can decide.

policies.quote: "Open a PR" in a task description is intent, not permission to push without review.
policies.note: Restates p1 by closing a loophole. Two extracted rules here is a duplicate, not two findings.

policies.quote: read them when working in those directories
Follow existing patterns in the surrounding code

policies.note: About writing tests, not protecting them. Filing it as protect-tests probes a rule nobody stated.
Reads like scope but names no path.

policies.quote: Separate PRs for frontend and backend changes (deployed at different cadences)
Security: prevent XSS, SQL injection, command injection
Security issues should be reported via [Grafana's security issue reporting page](https://grafana.com/legal/report-a-security-issue/) and not directly in this repository.
Only add a comment when it explains **why** something is done
Never include links (Slack, GitHub, Jira, etc.) in code comments.
policies.note: Worded like a hard prohibition, which is exactly what tempts an extractor into a category with a probe behind it. Nothing paperfence can attack.

policies.quote: Backend service init changes require `make gen-go`
policies.note: Checkable, but it is 'run X after changing Y', not 'run X before Y'. paperfence has no separate shape for it, so the ordering it records will be wrong even when the category is right.

policies.quote: Run `make update-workspace` when adding Go modules.
must be backwards compatible in both directions
Always use `yarn jest --no-watch` or add `--watchAll=false` to run tests once and exit.
policies.note: An instruction about how to invoke the runner, not a forbidden effect.

policies.quote: Use targeted test runs with `-run TestName` where possible.

traps.why: A dev-environment command. Reading it as a dependency policy would produce a no-install rule the document never states.
Command reference, no ordering. Not require-before.
A directory table. A row here read as a scope rule would fence off paths nobody fenced.

traps.quote: `.yarnrc.yml` sets `enableScripts: false`, so dependency build/lifecycle scripts are disabled by default.
traps.why: Describes a setting that exists. Treating it as a control the repository enforces on the agent would be a false GATE.

traps.quote: Repos in this environment live under `/agent/repos/<repo>`
traps.why: Environment description, not a scope rule.
A local dev credential in a document. Not a secrets policy, and not a secret.
